why.text: Glacial moraine soils with good drainage, a mild climate eased by Lake Iseo, and long ageing on the lees after bottle fermentation.

styles.text: Only bottle-fermented sparkling wine: Franciacorta, Satèn and Rosé, with vintage and Riserva versions.

climate.text: Insubrian mesoclimate with some Mediterranean traits, relatively mild in winter and not too hot in summer, with Lake Iseo easing temperatures. Rain is about 1000 mm a year, 500 to 600 mm in the growing season. Winkler index is 1800 to 2300 degree days.

soil.text: Mostly glacial moraine, fairly deep, well drained, with good or high water reserve. Six vocational units are named, from thin moraine to deep colluvium.

tastes.text: Straw yellow with green or gold glints, fine lasting bubbles, bread crust and yeast, citrus and dried nuts. Savoury, fresh, fine and harmonious.

styles.name: Satèn
styles.text: Creamy, only brut, at least 50% Chardonnay, max 5 atm, 24 months on lees.

styles.name: Rosé
styles.text: At least 35% Pinot nero, pink colour before bottling, 24 months on lees.

styles.name: Millesimato
styles.text: Vintage wine, at least 85% from that year, 30 months on lees.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: Vintage wine aged at least 60 months on the lees.

why.text: Sunny Apennine foothills on limestone and marl soils, with cold winters, warm summers and a spread of microclimates, give fresh, sapid sparkling wine.

styles.text: Only bottle-fermented sparkling wine, white or rosé, with or without Pinot nero as the named grape.

climate.text: Mean annual temperature is about 11 to 12 °C from the foot of the hills to 600 m, and January averages 1 to 2 °C. July or August average 22 to 24 °C. Rain peaks in November (143 mm) and is lowest in July (47 mm). South-facing slopes in the west often exceed 2,750 MJ/m2 of sun per year.

soil.text: Vineyards must be on calcareous or clay-limestone soils on sunny hillsides, never valley floors or plains. Geology is varied: marls, sandstones, limestones, clays and gypsum.

altitude.text: Temperature data run from the foot of the hills to 600 m. The 0 °C isotherm at about 800 m marks the limit between hill and mountain zones.

tastes.text: Fine, persistent foam; straw-yellow or pink; fine, gentle bouquet; sapid, fresh and harmonious. Pinot nero versions are well structured.

styles.name: Metodo classico
styles.text: Second fermentation in bottle; at least 15 months on the lees.

styles.name: Millesimato
styles.text: Vintage-dated wine; at least 24 months on the lees.

styles.name: Pinot nero
styles.text: At least 85% Pinot nero, with at least 12% alcohol.

styles.name: Rosé
styles.text: Pink version; on the label it may only be called rosé.

why.text: Steep marl hillsides with very thin soil and a Mediterranean-like climate; the grapes are dried for at least 21 days after harvest.

styles.text: One sweet red wine, made only from Moscato di Scanzo grapes dried after harvest.

climate.text: Typically Mediterranean, allowing good ripening of the vines; olive groves grow here too.

soil.text: Very shallow topsoil over marly rock called Sass de la Luna, which crumbles in the sun and forms hard limy nodules. Hill slopes run 50 to 100%, with a few exceptions.

tastes.text: Ruby red, sometimes cherry-toned with garnet reflections. Delicate, intense, lasting aroma. Sweet, pleasant and harmonious, with a light almond aftertaste.

styles.name: Scanzo / Moscato di Scanzo
styles.text: Sweet red from dried Moscato di Scanzo grapes, aged at least two years, no wood.

why.text: South-facing, steep, dry-stone terraces of sandy granitic soil, sheltered by the Alps, with Nebbiolo grapes dried through the winter to concentrate their sugar.

others: Other non-aromatic red grapes suited to Lombardy (up to 10%)

styles.text: A dry red made only from dried grapes, aged at least 20 months, at least 12 in wooden barrels.

climate.text: Alps shelter the valley, Lake Como moderates it; about 850 mm rain a year, over 1,900 sunshine hours, daytime air 5 to 35 °C in April to October, humidity 65 to 80%, day-night swings of 8 to 20 °C before harvest.

soil.text: Mostly sandy (about 70%) and silty (about 18%), no limestone, broken-down granite; very permeable, shallow (40 to 120 cm), drought-prone.

altitude.text: Vineyards run from 300 m up to 700 m on the south-facing slope; the zone limit is 700 m (600 m on the left bank).

tastes.text: Ruby red with possible garnet glints. Intense, broad aroma with hints of ripe fruit. Very soft, dry, structured and full of character, with possible oak notes.

styles.name: Sforzato / Sfursat
styles.text: Dried Nebbiolo grapes vinified from 1 December; at least 14% alcohol.

styles.name: Appassimento
styles.text: Grapes dried indoors, losing about 30% of their water, reaching 26 to 27% sugar.

why.text: South-facing, dry-stone terraces of granite sand at 300 to 700 m, sheltered by the Alps, give Nebbiolo strong sun and big day-night swings.

others: Other non-aromatic red grapes suited to Lombardy, up to 10%

styles.text: Dry red still wine, with five named subzones and a Riserva tier.

climate.text: Vines are shielded by the Rhaetian Alps to north and east, and Lake Como tempers temperatures. Rainfall averages 850 mm a year. Sunshine tops 1,900 hours a year. April to October daytime air runs +5 to +35 °C, with day-night swings of 8 to 20 °C before harvest. Vineyard air is 4 to 5 °C warmer than the valley floor.

soil.text: Mostly sandy (about 70%) and silty (about 18%), from broken-down granite, with no limestone. Very permeable, low in water retention and shallow, 40 to 120 cm workable depth.

altitude.text: Vineyards sit on the south-facing Rhaetian slope from 300 m up to 700 m, except two alluvial fans. Slopes can exceed 70%.

tastes.text: Ruby red turning garnet, with a characteristic, persistent, delicate scent. Dry, slightly tannic, velvety and harmonious.

styles.name: Riserva
styles.text: Aged at least three years.

styles.name: Sassella
styles.text: Subzone name; wine only from that subzone's vineyards.

styles.name: Grumello
styles.text: Subzone name; wine only from that subzone's vineyards.

styles.name: Inferno
styles.text: Subzone name; wine only from that subzone's vineyards.
